clue.text: Hungry actor getting part in dream play

definitions.meaning: an archaic noun for a starving, underfed creature, used here as the hungry one

definitions.text: actor getting part in dream play
definitions.meaning: Robin ... the tailor plays Moonshine in the mechanicals' play within A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A half-starved actor lands a role in a play about a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's mechanicals carry joke names; the tailor's name points at his thinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tailor is named for being thin and underfed, and the common noun means a starving wretch.

clue.text: Label base for Indian writer

parts.note: to label something is to tag it
ore is the raw base material from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A tag stuck on the bottom of a box marks it as the work of an Indian author.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabindranath Tagore was the Bengali poet and novelist who won the 1913 Nobel Prize for Literature.

clue.text: Eliot said that only a cock stood on it

definitions.text: Eliot said that only a cock stood on it

parts.words: Eliot said that only a cock stood on it
parts.note: in The Waste Land, What the Thunder Said, a cock crows from the top beam of the ruined chapel's roof

explanation.surface: A reminder of a famous line from T. S. Eliot about a lone cockerel.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridge beam along the top of a roof is where Eliot's cock perches in the empty chapel scene.

clue.text: Men's follows us according to the company we keep" (Richard Steele, Spectator)

definitions.text: Men's follows us according to the company we keep" (Richard Steele, Spectator)

parts.words: Men's follows us according to the company we keep" (Richard Steele, Spectator)
parts.note: a missing word in Steele's Spectator essay: others' judgement of us depends on the friends we keep

explanation.surface: A quotation from Steele with its key word removed, to be supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing noun is the regard or judgement in which people hold us, which Steele says depends on our companions.

clue.text: Shaw had it that Imogen wished her chest had smothered him

definitions.text: Shaw had it that Imogen wished her chest had smothered him

parts.words: Shaw had it that Imogen wished her chest had smothered him
parts.note: in Cymbeline the villain hides in a trunk in Imogen's bedroom; Shaw's Cymbeline Refinished jokes about it

explanation.surface: Shaw imagines a heroine wishing her luggage had suffocated a stowaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian schemer of Cymbeline smuggles himself into Imogen's room inside a chest to spy on her.

clue.text: A way out offered by Cecil Day Lewis

definitions.meaning: an opening in a fence or wall through which one leaves
Day Lewis published a late collection called The ..., and Other Poems (1962)

explanation.surface: A poet laureate offers an escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening in a wall or fence is an exit, and it names a Day Lewis poetry collection.

clue.text: Not Chesterton's Man Friday, surely?

parts.note: Chesterton's anarchist thriller is The Man Who Was a weekday, and Friday is the wrong one; Crusoe's servant is the false lead

explanation.surface: A doubtful query about whether Chesterton wrote about Crusoe's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's novel The Man Who Was ... names its hero, Syme, after the day before Friday.

clue.text: Novel situation of the Jarndyce estate?

definitions.meaning: the second book of Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga
in Bleak House the Jarndyce fortune is tied up for years in the court of equity

explanation.surface: A question about where Dickens's disputed inheritance stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy titled a Forsyte novel after the legal phrase for property held in the Lord Chancellor's court, as Dickens's Jarndyce estate was.

clue.text: Leery concerning old Greek magistrate

parts.note: arch, like leery, means knowing and sly
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is suspicious about an ancient Athenian official.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Athens the chief magistrates, nine each year, held this title.

clue.text: Leslie Stephen an apologetic one

parts.note: Stephen wrote the essay collection An ... Apology (1893), so he was an apologist of this kind

explanation.surface: Virginia Woolf's father described as somebody sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apologetic' means offering an apologia, a defence of one's belief, not saying sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen defended doubt about God's existence in An Agnostic's Apology, making him an unbeliever with a defence.

clue.text: *The princely — In their bright stand there left his Powers to seize / Possession of the Garden" (Milton, Paradise Lost)

definitions.text: *The princely — In their bright stand there left his Powers to seize / Possession of the Garden" (Milton, Paradise Lost)

parts.words: *The princely — In their bright stand there left his Powers to seize / Possession of the Garden" (Milton, Paradise Lost)
parts.note: the missing word is Milton's title for the archangel Michael, who leaves his troops to take over Eden

explanation.surface: A Milton passage about the angels expelling Adam and Eve, with its key word blanked.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief priest or ruler of a sacred order, Milton's title for Michael as the leader of heaven's host.

clue.text: Earl may be mistaken for king

indicators.note: something mistaken has gone wrong, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman is confused with a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's old British king who divides his realm among his daughters.

clue.text: "Vale of Friendship " of Lady Eleanor and the Hon. Sarah

definitions.text: "Vale of Friendship " of Lady Eleanor and the Hon. Sarah

parts.words: "Vale of Friendship " of Lady Eleanor and the Hon. Sarah
parts.note: Lady Eleanor Butler and Sarah Ponsonby, the Ladies of the Welsh vale, lived together at Plas Newydd

explanation.surface: The valley home of two famous eighteenth-century ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh town in the Dee valley where the two Irish ladies set up house together in 1780.

clue.text: A scrap of Leon Uris

parts.note: Uris wrote a 1964 novel of Berlin named after the final battle of Revelation; a scrap is a fight

explanation.surface: A fragment of an American bestseller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fragment, but it is a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The last great battle of Revelation, the title of a Uris novel about the Berlin airlift.

clue.text: Shakespeare put him in the pit

definitions.text: Shakespeare put him in the pit

parts.words: Shakespeare put him in the pit
parts.note: the cheap standing spectators in the yard of the Globe, whose ears Hamlet says are split by ranting actors

explanation.surface: Shakespeare banishes someone to a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A playgoer who stood in the pit or yard of an Elizabethan theatre, mocked in Hamlet.

clue.text: Diana merits a whole new look

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: giving the letters a whole new look means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A princess deserves a complete makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is the Roman counterpart of the Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

clue.text: Some dramaturge, never seen as such, becomes novelist

indicators.note: some of the following words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A playwright who never gets seen as one turns to fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen as such' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was the Russian author of Fathers and Sons, who also wrote plays.

clue.text: Prescience said to be associated with Soames

indicators.note: said to be signals the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: prescience is foresight, knowing what will come

explanation.surface: Prophetic insight is linked with a man named Soames.
explanation.definitionFit: Soames is the possessive solicitor at the centre of Galsworthy's family saga, whose surname this is.

clue.text: CEO, Tree Preservation Society?

parts.note: the Roman god of woods and fields imagined as head of a forest conservation body

explanation.surface: A job title for the boss of a tree-protection charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity who guarded forests and uncultivated land is jokingly cast as head of a society saving woods.

clue.text: What Symons did for Rolfe

parts.note: A. J. A. Symons wrote The Quest for Corvo, a search for the life of Frederick Rolfe

explanation.surface: A question about one writer's service to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Symons searched for the facts of Rolfe's life in The Quest for Corvo, so he went looking for him.

clue.text: Giant success of Alcofribas Nasier

parts.note: Alcofribas Nasier was Rabelais's pen name, an anagram of his own; his hit was a book about a giant

explanation.surface: A huge triumph for a strangely named writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant' reads as 'huge', but it also names the subject of Rabelais's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous, from the giant Gargantua of Rabelais, whose first books appeared under the pen name Alcofribas Nasier.

clue.text: Hume's lacked provenance

parts.note: Fergus Hume wrote The ... from Nowhere (1900), a woman whose origin is unknown

explanation.surface: A philosopher's work is suspected of being of unknown origin.
explanation.walkthrough: David Hume the philosopher is the false lead; this is Fergus Hume, the detective novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Fergus Hume's title figure is a woman from nowhere, a gentlewoman with no known origin.

clue.text: Blue feature of Chandler screenplay

parts.note: Raymond Chandler wrote the 1946 film The Blue ...

explanation.surface: Something blue in a film script by a crime writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chandler's only original screenplay is named after a blue-coloured garden flower, which features in its title.

clue.text: Styron suggested obscurity for one such

definitions.text: Styron suggested obscurity for one such

parts.words: Styron suggested obscurity for one such
parts.note: William Styron's first novel was Lie Down in Darkness, a rest taken in obscurity

explanation.surface: An American novelist recommends darkness for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Short rests taken lying flat, one of which Styron's title sets in darkness.

clue.text: Marie Corelli's sort of wood

parts.note: Corelli's 1890 novel ... is about absinthe addiction

explanation.surface: The kind of timber a Victorian novelist favoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Corelli's novel title joins this crawling creature to wood, naming the bitter herb used in absinthe.

clue.text: Integral sort of romantic novel situation

indicators.note: a sort of the word, out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Love-triangle plots are a core part of romantic fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair involving three people is the classic plot of romantic fiction.

clue.text: Late bypass for Shakespearian duke

parts.note: the duke in Henry V shares his name with the Devon city whose road bypass is notorious for holiday traffic

explanation.surface: A nobleman from Shakespeare is held up on a ring road.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Duke of Exeter, uncle of Henry V, takes his title from the Devon cathedral city.

clue.text: Isle of Davenant

parts.note: William Davenant's 1638 poem collection was titled after the large island off south-east Africa

explanation.surface: An island associated with a Restoration playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island in the Indian Ocean off Africa, the title of Davenant's poem on Prince Rupert.
